Comments: No credible evidence found that the digital CRVS pilot explicitly includes non-citizens (e.g., foreign residents/refugees) in scope; sources describe citizen access to request copies and do not specify inclusion categories.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (None) is not supported by the cited source: the territoire.gouv.tg article concerns online delivery of civil-status copies and does not address non-citizen eligibility at all. Togo's 2009 Law on Civil Status, Article 3, explicitly requires a civil status act for every birth, marriage and death of any person 'de nationalité togolaise ou étrangère résidant au Togo' (Togolese or foreign national resident in Togo), with no restriction to permanent residents. Revised to 4 (All included) on the strength of this primary legislation. Some practical gaps remain — the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child (2023) flagged incomplete birth registration and statelessness/nationality risks for children of refugee parents — but these are uptake/implementation issues, not a restriction on the legal scope of who may be registered.
revised_comments: Togo's Law on Civil Status (2009), Article 3, requires that a civil status act be drawn up for every birth, marriage and death of any person, whether of Togolese or foreign nationality, who is resident in Togo, with no restriction to citizens or to permanent residents. In practice, registration completeness varies by region, family income and education, and the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child has raised concerns about barriers to nationality and residual statelessness risk for children of refugee parents, but the legal scope of civil registration extends to all residents regardless of nationality.

revision_notes: Moved from fast path after a light search surfaced authoritative World Bank programme documentation with quantified coverage data. Original score of 0/Unknown lacked a source; revised to 1 (<20%) based on the World Bank ASTRE (P178835) Programme-for-Results Disbursement-Linked Indicator baseline for share of population registered in the dynamic social registry (RSPM), recorded as effectively 0% as at 30-Sep-2024, against a target of at least 50% of households by around 2028, plus reporting of 142,722 beneficiaries reached under a predecessor scheme (Aug 2024–Aug 2025) against a stated target population of over 700,000 vulnerable people.
revised_comments: Togo's dynamic Social Registry of Persons and Households (RSPM), developed by the National Identification Agency (ANID) with World Bank WURI/ASTRE support, was at an early stage of rollout as of late 2024: the programme's disbursement-linked coverage indicator recorded a baseline of effectively 0% of the population registered as at September 2024, against a target of registering at least 50% of households by around 2028. A predecessor cash-transfer scheme reached some 142,722 beneficiaries between August 2024 and August 2025, against a stated target of more than 700,000 vulnerable people, implying that current coverage of the intended beneficiary population remains well below 20%.

Revised from 0/Unknown to 4 (Partially integrated): registration events and identifiers (RCCM number and NIF) are issued together through the CFE one-stop shop, though a 2019 African Development Bank-financed procurement notice for further automated data exchange between OTR, SIGFiP, CFE and INSEED suggests deeper systemic/API-level interoperability may still be maturing, short of 'fully integrated nationwide'.
revised_comments: Business registration in Togo is handled through the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) one-stop shop, which issues a single 'carte unique de création d'entreprise' bearing both the RCCM (trade and business register) number and the NIF (tax identification number) simultaneously. The CFE and RCCM databases have been interconnected since January 2019, allowing shared access to registration records, so that CFE registration also triggers tax registration with the Office Togolais des Recettes (OTR).

revised_comments: Togo's tax identification number (Numéro d'Identifiant Fiscal, NIF), issued by the Office Togolais des Recettes (OTR), is a separate credential from the national biometric identity system (NIU/e-ID) run by the National Identification Agency (ANID). Research on OTR's digital transformation confirms the NIF is not issued automatically as part of the national identification process; taxpayers must separately provide identity documents and other details during tax registration, with no automated linkage between the two identifiers.
